title: Sherpa Tensing — Descent One: Present Continuous Passive (B1)
description: The longest thing you will say in ordinary English without anyone noticing: is being done. Three words to say that something is happening to a thing at…

hero.lede: The longest thing you will say in ordinary English without anyone noticing: is being done. Three words to say that something is happening to a thing at this moment, and that whoever is doing it is not what the sentence is about.

sections.label: Descent briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: The passive is not a different tense. It is the present continuous with the doer let go — and the reason you let them go is always one of these six.

cards.head: You do not know who
cards.body: Nobody can tell you the doer, so the sentence does without one.

cards.head: The doer does not matter
cards.body: The event is the news; who did it is a footnote.
cards.ex: "My car is being repaired at the moment."

cards.head: The doer is obvious
cards.body: Saying it would be a waste of everyone's time.

cards.head: You would rather not say
cards.body: The passive is how English removes a person from a sentence.

cards.head: Putting the important thing first
cards.body: Whatever you put at the front is what the sentence is about.

cards.head: Putting the doer back with by
cards.body: When the doer is the point, it goes at the end.
cards.ex: "The kitchen is being redone by a firm from Leeds."

cards.head: Affirmative
cards.body: subject + am / is / are + being + past participle

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: the not goes after the first auxiliary

cards.head: Questions
cards.body: the first auxiliary moves to the front

cards.head: With the doer
cards.ex: "It is being handled by the duty team."

charts.head: Turning an active sentence around
charts.note: Three moves, always the same: the object comes to the front, the verb becomes am / is / are + being + participle, and the old subject either disappears or goes to the back behind by. Only the middle step changes from camp to camp.

head: Active
Passive
What moved
rows: A firm from Leeds is redoing the kitchen.
The kitchen is being redone by a firm from Leeds.
The firm stayed, at the end.

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Being never changes and never leaves. Only am, is or are moves, and the participle sits behind both of them.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this one is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: The road is not doing the resurfacing. Without being the sentence says it is.
Been belongs to the perfect. The continuous takes being.
I am being knowing him for years.
I have known him for years.
State verbs refuse the continuous, active or passive.

charts.note: Neither is better. The question is only what the sentence is about — because whatever you put at the front is what the reader will think it is about.

head: Question
Passive
Active
rows:
The thing it happens to.
"The road is being resurfaced."

The one who does it.
"They are resurfacing the road."
Often not — and you do not need to.
Yes, and you are naming them.
At the end with by, or nowhere at all.
At the front, as the subject.
Longer by two or three words.
Usually shorter. Prefer it when both work.

charts.example: Listen for it in the news and in bad news generally: the matter is being looked into, steps are being taken, your call is being held in a queue. Three words that promise activity while naming nobody at all — which is exactly why it is worth being able to hear.

sections.label: Trail markers
sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: Verbs with no passive at all

sections.example: The test for whether a verb can go passive: does it take an object? They built it has one, so it turns. It happened has none, so it cannot.

sections.label: Interactive
sections.title: The event, and the doer you dropped

diagram.intro: The block is the same block as the ascent, lit from above instead of fading into the dark — because the tense has not changed, only the light. Inside it sits a dashed box: the doer. It is drawn inside the event rather than beside it because the doer is not a moment in time, it is a part of the sentence — and it is dashed because most of the time nobody says it. Click either to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: The doer — optional, and usually gone
items: … and notice that nobody is making them.

quiz.explain: Is + being + participle. Is resurfacing would say the road is doing it.
The car is not repairing anything. Is being repaired.
Wards is plural, so are being, and the participle of build is built.
The not goes after are, then being, then the participle.
Is + subject + being + participle. Room is singular.
The phrasal verb keeps its preposition at the end: is being looked into.
Last summer is a finished past time, so the past simple passive.
I takes am, then being, then watched.
Is being questioned puts it in progress at this moment.
Are being made. Note how completely the passive removes the decider.

quiz.prompt: The kitchen _____ by a firm from Leeds. (redo)
quiz.explain: Is being redone, with the doer at the end behind by.
Hold / held / held. The passive lets the company off naming itself.
Are being moved says it is happening to us; are moving would say we are doing it.
Are being taken. Take / took / taken.

results: Clean run. You can turn a sentence around and you know when the doer is worth keeping.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at the active version before you go on.
Good first attempt. The auxiliary chain is the part to read again.
